newsitem.title: UK: IGC sharply lifts 1996 coarse grain crop, stocks.
newsitem.headline: IGC sharply lifts 1996 coarse grain crop, stocks.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Tuesday revised up its estimate for 1996 world coarse grains output to a record 884 million tonnes from the previous forecast of 875 million due to a larger U.S. maize crop.
The figure compares with the 1995 outturn estimated at 796 million tonnes.

In its latest monthly report, the IGC pegged the U.S. coarse grain production at 267 million tonnes, up from last month's estimate of 260.4 million. Maize was raised to 235 million tonnes from 229 million due to better yields.
Another sharp increase occurred in the estimate for China which the IGC put at 128 million tonnes from last month's 124 million tonnes.
As a result of higher U.S. production, the IGC sharply raised the estimate for end-season (July 1997) stocks to 114 million tonnes from 105 million projected last month.
The new stocks figure compared with the 20-year-low of 87 million tonnes in 1995/96.
World trade in coarse grains was seen down by one million tonnes at 88 million tonnes mainly due to lower imports of sorghum by Mexico.
The production estimate for the European Union (EU) was further raised in November to 104.5 million tonnes from last month's 102.9 million due to better maize crops in France, Germany and Italy.

In the former Soviet Union, the estimates for Kazakhstan and Russia were reduced to 4.7 million tonnes and 35.5 million tonnes respectively from last month's 5.8 million and 38.5 million tonnes. Russia's barley crop was down due to lower yields.
Argentina was up by one million tonnes to 16.1 million tonnes due to favourable weather and an increase in plantings.
A record barley outturn was expected in Canada this year but maize was lower than expected. In Brazil, a 10-percent increase in maize output from the 1995 level was possible as drought has abated.
Australia's harvest was progessing well in most regions but the crop estimate was unchanged from last month's 9.6 million tonnes.
